'''Mikhail&nbsp;Iosiphovich Kadets''' ({{langx|ru|Михаил Иосифович Кадец}}, {{langx|uk|Михайло Йосипович Кадець }},  sometimes transliterated as '''Kadec''', 30 November 1923 – 7 March 2011) was a Soviet-born Jewish mathematician working in [[mathematical analysis|analysis]] and the theory of [[Banach space]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|mr=2829617|title=In memory of Mikhail Iosifovich Kadets (1923–2011)|journal=Zh. Mat. Fiz. Anal. Geom.|volume= 7 |year=2011|issue=2|pages=194–195|language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|journal=Russ. Math. Surv. |volume=66|issue=4|pages=809|year=2011|doi=10.1070/RM2011v066n04ABEH004756|title=Mikhail Iosifovich Kadets (obituary)|first1=Yurii&nbsp;I. |last1=Lyubich|author-link1=Yurii Lyubich|first2=Vladimir&nbsp;A.|last2= Marchenko|first3=Sergei&nbsp;P.|last3= Novikov|author-link3=Sergei Novikov (mathematician)|first4=M.&nbsp;I.|last4=Ostrovskii|first5=Leonid&nbsp;A.|last5= Pastur|first6=Anatolii&nbsp;N.|last6= Plichko|first7=M.&nbsp;M.|last7=Popov|first8=Evgenii&nbsp;M.|last8= Semenov|first9=S.&nbsp;L.|last9=Troyanskii|first10=Vladimir&nbsp;P.|last10= Fonf|first11=Evgenii&nbsp;Ya.|last11= Khruslov|bibcode=2011RuMaS..66..809L |s2cid=122568537 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|mr=0771114|last1=Gelʹfand|first1=I.&nbsp;M.|last2=Levin|first2=B.&nbsp;Ya.|last3=Marchenko|first3=V.&nbsp;A.|last4=Pogorelov|first4=A.&nbsp;V.|last5=Sobolev|first5=S.&nbsp;L.|title=Mikhail&nbsp;Iosifovich Kadets (on the occasion of his sixtieth birthday)|journal=Russian Math. Surveys|volume=39 |year=1984|issue=6|pages=231–232|doi=10.1070/rm1984v039n06abeh003197|s2cid=250861162 }}</ref>

==Life and work==
Kadets was born in [[Kyiv]]. In 1943, he was drafted into the army. After demobilisation in 1946, he studied at [[Kharkov University]], graduating in 1950. After several years in [[Makeevka]] he returned to Kharkov in 1957, where he spent the remainder of his life working at various institutes. He defended his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1955 (under the supervision of [[Boris Levin]]), and his doctoral dissertation in 1963.  He was awarded the State Prize of Ukraine in 2005.

After reading the Ukrainian translation of [[Stefan Banach|Banach]]'s monograph ''[[Théorie des Opérations Linéaires]]'',<ref>The French original {{cite book|jfm=58.0420.01|last=Banach|first=S.|author-link=Stefan Banach|title=Theory of Linear Operations|location=Warszawa|publisher=Mathematisches Seminar der Univ. Warschau|series= Monografje Matematyczne I|year=1932}} was translated as {{cite book|last=Banach|first=S.|location=Kiev|year=1948|language=uk|title=Course in functional analysis|publisher=Radians'ka shkola}}</ref> he became interested in the theory of Banach spaces.<ref>{{harvtxt|Ostrovskii|Plichko|2009|loc=First page of preprint}}: {{cite journal|mr=2597043|last1=Ostrovskii|first1=M. I.|last2=Plichko|first2=A. M.|title=On the Ukrainian translation of ''Théorie des opérations linéaires'' and Mazur's updates of the "remarks" section|journal=Mat. Stud.|volume= 32|year=2009|issue=1|pages=96–111|url=http://facpub.stjohns.edu/ostrovsm/OstrovskiiPlichko.pdf}}</ref> In 1966, Kadets solved in the affirmative the [[Stefan Banach|Banach]]–[[Maurice René Fréchet|Fréchet]] problem, asking whether every two [[separable space|separable]] infinite-dimensional  Banach spaces are [[homeomorphism|homeomorphic]]. He developed the method of equivalent norms, which has found numerous applications. For example, he showed that every separable Banach space admits an equivalent [[Fréchet derivative|Fréchet differentiable]] norm if and only if the [[dual space]] is separable.<ref name=pietsch>{{cite book|mr=2300779|last=Pietsch|first=Albrecht|title=History of Banach spaces and linear operators|publisher=Birkhäuser Boston, Inc.|location=Boston, MA|year=2007|isbn=978-0-8176-4367-6|page=609}}</ref>

Together with [[Aleksander Pełczyński]], he obtained important results on the topological structure of [[Lp space]]s.<ref>{{cite book|mr=0889253|last=Beauzamy|first=Bernard|title=Introduction to Banach spaces and their geometry|edition=2nd|series=North-Holland Mathematics Studies|volume=68|publisher=North-Holland Publishing Co.|location=Amsterdam|year=1985|isbn=0-444-87878-5 |chapter=Chapter VI}}</ref>

Kadets also made several contributions to the theory of finite-dimensional normed spaces. Together with M.&nbsp;G.&nbsp;Snobar (1971), he showed that every <math>n</math>-dimensional subspace of a Banach space is the image of a projection of norm at most <math>\sqrt{n}.</math><ref>{{cite book|mr=2766381|last1=Fabian|first1=Marián|last2=Habala|first2=Petr|last3=Hájek|first3=Petr|last4=Montesinos|first4=Vicente|last5=Zizler|first5=Václav|title=Banach&nbsp;space theory. The basis for linear and nonlinear analysis|series=CMS Books in Mathematics/Ouvrages de Mathématiques de la SMC|publisher=Springer|location=New York|year=2011|isbn=978-1-4419-7514-0|pages=320–323}}</ref> Together with [[Vladimir Gurariy|V.&nbsp;I.&nbsp;Gurarii]] and V.&nbsp;I.&nbsp;Matsaev, he found the exact order of magnitude of the [[Banach–Mazur distance]] between the <math>n</math>-dimensional spaces <math>\ell^n_p</math> and <math>\ell^n_q.</math><ref>{{cite book|mr=0993774|last=Tomczak-Jaegermann|first=Nicole|author-link=Nicole Tomczak-Jaegermann|title=Banach-Mazur distances and finite-dimensional operator ideals|series= Pitman Monographs and Surveys in Pure and Applied Mathematics|volume=38|publisher=Longman Scientific & Technical|location=Harlow|year=1989|isbn=0-582-01374-7|page=138}}</ref>

In [[harmonic analysis]], Kadets proved (1964) what is now called the Kadets&nbsp;<math>1/4</math> theorem, which states that, if <math>|\lambda_n - n| \leq C < 1/4</math> for all integers <math>n,</math> then the sequence <math>(\exp(i \lambda_n x))_{n \in \Z}</math> is a [[Riesz sequence|Riesz basis]] in <math>L_2[-\pi, \pi]</math><ref>{{cite book|mr=0499341|last=Higgins|first=John Rowland|title=Completeness and basis&nbsp;properties of sets of special functions|series=Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics|volume=72|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge-New York-Melbourne|year=1977|isbn=0-521-21376-2}}</ref>

Kadets was the founder of the [[Kharkiv|Kharkov]] school of Banach spaces.<ref name=pietsch/>

Together with his son Vladimir Kadets, he authored two books about series in Banach spaces.<ref>
{{cite book|last1=Kadets|first1=Mikhail I.|last2=Kadets|first2=Vladimir M.|title=Series in Banach spaces: Conditional and unconditional convergence| edition=Translated by Andrei Iacob from the Russian-language|series=Operator Theory: Advances and Applications|volume=94|publisher=Birkhäuser Verlag|location=Basel|year=1997|pages=viii+156|isbn=3-7643-5401-1|mr=1442255}}
</ref>
